Subject: Request: subprocessor custody, KMS residency, and escrow details for SIG/CAIQ mapping

Hi Rachel,

We're kicking off HealthGrid's SIG-lite assessment and need a concise package from Redwood covering: a) canonical subprocessor roster with clear ownership/custody annotations (who owns the data flow vs who executes compute), b) KMS residency (regions & providers used for customer key material), and c) any escrow/third-party custody arrangements for critical artifacts (code, model checkpoints, or keys).

Can you provide a short CSV manifest and a short narrative that maps to the SIG/CAIQ controls (encryption/residency, key custody, subprocessors)? We're aiming to ingest artifacts into our tracking tool by 2026-12-15. If you can flag anything that needs legal/contract review (escrow clause, residency exceptions), call that out.

Attachments requested: SIG-lite questionnaire reference (we'll attach on our side) and any existing subprocessor inventory.

Thanks — Gwen
Gwen Park
Security Program Manager, HealthGrid

---
Note: We are particularly interested in the custody distinction for ephemeral keys vs managed KMS, and whether any subprocessor can access plaintext for debugging or support.

Rachel / team — attaching the latest manifest export and inline notes.

Key highlights (short):
- Ownership: columns Owner=team responsible for dataflow (e.g., Serving Runtime, Telemetry, Billing). Custody=service that stores or processes customer artifacts.
- Onshore-hosted critical dependencies: KeyVaultInc (KMS wrapping service) — custody for wrapping keys, no plaintext access to long-term customer secrets.
- Ephemeral providers: FastBatch (inference prefetch caching) — only sees tokenized payloads; no access to persistent plaintext.
- Model checkpoints: Redwood-managed private artifact store; legal escrow only for customer-requested model snapshots (rare; require DPA addendum).

Adding KMS residency details for the packet. Short summary: 
- Customer key material: primary KMS providers are AWS KMS (us-west-2) and GCP KMS (europe-west1) depending on customer region.
- Key roles: Customer-managed CMKs via BYOK are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API customers use Redwood-managed KMS with per-tenant key separation.
- Access controls: Only the KMS provider and Redwood's key-management service have cryptographic metadata necessary for routing; no Redwood employee has access to unwrapped customer plaintext unless explicit emergency unwrap is performed via documented break-glass (requires 4-eyes + audit).
- Telemetry: KMS audit logs are retained per our retention policy (see kms_residency_report.pdf).

Attachment stub: kms_residency_report.pdf
Link to policies: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Subproc-Inventory/policies

Gwen — please find the draft package below and attachments. We focused on mapping evidence to the SIG-lite controls you referenced.

Included (draft):
- subprocessor_manifest_v2.csv (owner/custody/residency_notes)
- kms_residency_report.pdf (regions, retention, BYOK support)
- short narrative mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls (embedded in email body)

High-level narrative excerpt: Redwood separates ownership (who defines the dataflow and SLA) from custody (who stores/processes data). Our serving runtime executes inference inside ephemeral containers; caching and temporary KV stores are accessed by FastBatch (no persistent plaintext). Key wrapping is performed by KeyVaultInc where used; long-term storage of customer artifacts is in Redwood's private artifact store. Emergency unwraps are strictly controlled and logged (4-eyes + legal). Model escrow is not enabled by default; if HealthGrid requests escrow of specific checkpoints we will require an addendum to the DPA and a scoped SOW.

Next steps: Monica from Legal — can you review the suggested escrow redline below and confirm whether we should propose a one-way escrow (customer-only retrieval) or a bilateral escrow with joint custody?

Proposed delivery date to HealthGrid: 2026-12-15 (final). If you want the manifest and KMS report sooner, we can push them by 2026-12-10.

Thanks,
Rachel
